## Profile

I develop computational statistical methods for model diagnostics and uncertainty quantification, with a focus on latent-state models, directional data and density estimation. My work connects statistical methodology, simulation, visualization and reproducible R software. My experience combines research, university teaching in French and English, academic coordination and data science leadership in industry.

## Education

- 2024\. PhD in Statistics, Université Laval. Dissertation: *General Multi-State Models for the Analysis of Animal Movement*. Supervisors: Thierry Duchesne and Louis-Paul Rivest. [Dissertation](https://corpus.ulaval.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/cf3426a4-3475-4d48-a4c4-de29df846ed5/content).
- 2010-2013. MSc in Probability and Statistics, Université Toulouse III. Thesis on random matrices and the smallest singular value.
- 2007-2010. BSc in Mathematics, Université Toulouse III.

## Academic and professional experience

- Since 2022. Université Laval, Department of Mathematics and Statistics: *chargé d’enseignement* (permanent teaching appointment) and coordinator of the Mathematics and Statistics Help and Learning Centre (CDA).
- Since 2021. Université du Québec à Chicoutimi: lecturer in statistics, data science and programming; supervision of undergraduate internships and research projects.
- 2020-2022. Co-operators: Director, Research and Analytics Innovation; led data science projects and created the Innovation Space in partnership with UQAC.
- 2017-2020. GSK Canada: Data Science Manager; process modelling, data governance and traceability in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
- 2014-2017. Université Laval: statistical consultant for research teams across several faculties.

## Research themes

- Sequential models: hidden Markov models, step-selection functions, generative validation and uncertainty in latent states.
- Directional statistics: angular regression, random-effects models and visualization of dependence.
- Density diagnostics: leave-one-out influence, outlier detection and grid-based computation.

[Research program and reproducible materials](https://aureliennicosiaulaval.github.io/web_site/en/recherche.html).

## Software and open resources

### Packages released on CRAN

- [CircularRegression](https://cran.r-project.org/package=CircularRegression): circular regression.
- [ggcircular](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ggcircular): circular, axial and directional visualization with ggplot2.
- [GLBFP](https://cran.r-project.org/package=GLBFP): density estimation with linear-blend frequency polygons. Leave-one-out diagnostics are in the GitHub development version.
- [tutorizeR](https://cran.r-project.org/package=tutorizeR): interactive tutorial creation from R Markdown or Quarto.
- [DonutMap](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DonutMap): donut-chart mapping.
- [GeneralOaxaca](https://cran.r-project.org/package=GeneralOaxaca): generalized Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition.

### Projects released on GitHub

- [learnrTrackR](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/learnrTrackR): tracking and export of interactive tutorial attempts.
- [leaflet.indoor](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/leaflet-indoor): experimental multi-level indoor mapping package.
- [lmmix](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/lmmix): Gaussian mixed models with correlated residuals, under development.
- [UlavalSSD](https://github.com/AurelienNicosiaULaval/UlavalSSD): Quebec datasets and introductory data science tools.
- [Données bleues](https://aureliennicosiaulaval.github.io/donnees-bleues/): Quebec and Canadian datasets with reproducible teaching activities.

## Teaching and academic coordination

- Université Laval: STT-1100, Introduction to Data Science; STT-2200, Data Analysis; STT-4230/STT-6230, Programming for Data Science; STT-1900, Statistics for Engineering; STT-2920, Probability for Engineering; MQT-2101, Data Analysis and Modelling.
- GSO-6092, *Project Management*, graduate level: taught in English in Winter 2026 and Fall 2026 (in progress).
- GSO-6082, Gestion de projets, graduate level: partial replacement assignment of 21 teaching hours, August 31 to October 16, 2026 (in progress).
